skill.name: observability-monitoring
skill.description: Implement logging, metrics, tracing, health checks, and Prometheus alerting for service reliability.
skill.summary: Build practical observability patterns for production services.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: External command findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, inline code, and a commented logging example. Environment findings are benign configuration reads, and the tracing URL defaults to localhost. One semantic privacy issue remains because templates log identifiers, amounts, stack traces, and trace attributes without redaction guidance.

remediation.issue: Sensitive identifiers and error details may enter logs and traces.
remediation.suggestion: Add redaction guidance and examples that avoid raw user IDs, order IDs, payment metadata, amounts, and stack traces in shared telemetry.

remediation.issue: Telemetry export destination depends on deployment configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Document that OTLP endpoints must be trusted, access controlled, and paired with retention and data minimization policies.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Sensitive Telemetry Exposure
semantic_findings.description: Logging examples include userId, orderId, order amount, stack traces, and payment.method without redaction or retention guidance. Adopted directly, this can expose personal or commercial data in log stores and trace exporters.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited templates explicitly record identifiers, amounts, stack traces, and payment metadata. The risk depends on deployment data policy, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Production services fail silently when logs, metrics, traces, and alerts are incomplete. This skill provides practical templates for service visibility and incident response.
actual_capabilities: Guides Winston structured logging with request IDs and response logging.
Provides Prometheus examples for HTTP, business, database, and cache metrics.
Shows OpenTelemetry setup with auto-instrumentation and manual spans.
Includes liveness, readiness, and startup health check endpoint patterns.
Provides Prometheus alerting rules for outages, errors, latency, memory, and cache health.
Offers an observability checklist for logs, metrics, traces, alerts, and dashboards.
limitations: Templates require adaptation to your framework, dependencies, and production data policy.
It does not deploy monitoring infrastructure or configure hosted vendor accounts.
Examples focus on TypeScript, Prometheus, Winston, and OpenTelemetry patterns.
Alert thresholds must be tuned against real traffic and service objectives.

use_cases.title: Add Service Visibility
use_cases.description: Add request logging, correlation IDs, health endpoints, and baseline metrics to a backend service.

use_cases.title: Improve Incident Response
use_cases.description: Create alerts and dashboards that reveal outages, error spikes, latency, and dependency failures.

use_cases.title: Standardize Platform Telemetry
use_cases.description: Define common logging, metrics, and tracing patterns for multiple services and teams.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Service Logging
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design structured request logging for my Express service. Include request IDs, log levels, and fields to avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Metrics and Health Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to propose Prometheus metrics and health checks for my API. Cover rate, errors, duration, dependencies, and readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Distributed Tracing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan OpenTelemetry tracing for request flow across my services. Include span names, attributes, and privacy safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Observability
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my production observability plan. Identify gaps in logs, metrics, traces, alerts, dashboards, and incident response.

output_examples.input: Add health checks for a service that depends on PostgreSQL and Redis.
output: Liveness confirms the process is running.
Readiness checks PostgreSQL and Redis latency before receiving traffic.
Startup returns unavailable until initialization is complete.

output_examples.input: Design alerts for a public API with latency and error problems.
output: Critical alerts cover service outages and sustained server error rates.
High alerts cover slow p95 request latency.
Medium alerts cover cache degradation and early error-rate increases.

output_examples.input: Review a logging plan before production launch.
output: Use structured events with request IDs and service metadata.
Redact personal data, secrets, payment data, and long request bodies.
Separate debug detail from production logs to control cost and exposure.

best_practices: Redact secrets, personal data, payment data, and full request bodies before logs or traces leave the service.
Keep metric labels low-cardinality so dashboards and storage remain stable.
Tie alerts to user impact, service objectives, and documented response actions.
anti_patterns: Logging tokens, passwords, payment details, full request bodies, or unbounded error payloads.
Using user IDs, order IDs, or raw paths as high-cardinality metric labels.
Creating noisy alerts for every warning without an impact threshold or owner.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design logging, metrics, tracing, health checks, and alerts for backend services.

faq.question: Does it support OpenTelemetry?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a TypeScript OpenTelemetry setup with auto-instrumentation and manual span examples.

faq.question: Does it include Prometheus examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Prometheus metrics and alerting rule examples for common service reliability signals.

faq.question: Can it deploy my monitoring stack?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and templates, but deployment remains your responsibility.

faq.question: How should I handle sensitive data?
faq.answer: Review all log and trace fields, then redact secrets, personal data, and payment data before export.

faq.question: Which users benefit most from this skill?
faq.answer: Backend engineers, site reliability engineers, and platform teams can use it to improve service visibility.
